quest.title: Wisdom Has Built Her House, She Has Hewn Out Her Seven Pillars
quest.description: Katheryne of the Sumeru Adventurers' Guild seems to be looking for you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Tanit Tribe Scout
dialogues.text: Hey! Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Bandits!

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Bandits? How rude! I am Mendas, a scout! And this is Hugeweh.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We are adventurers just passing by.

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Here... the Matriarch has forbidden us from harming foreign adventurers, you must hurry up and get out of here!

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Gah. If only Jeht were here. She's better at dealing with outsiders...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Did you say Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Well, what's the matter, then? She joined us some time back and is highly valued by the Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: She's practically the Matriarch's shadow... Hmph, none of us tribespeople even come close to that kind of treatment.

choices.text: We actually kind of know her.

response.speaker: Mendas
response.text: Well, if you're Jeht's friends, I won't stop you. You may move on. The tribe's campsite lies ahead.

response.speaker: Mendas
response.text: Jeht isn't back yet, but Aderfi, Masseira, and Yuften are in at the moment. They're pretty friendly to outsiders.

response.speaker: Mendas
response.text: You can look for them... But if you have lied to us, you will find us less merciful.

choices.text: We're supposed to be her friends.

dialogues.text: B—But... I don't know what those outsiders wanted... It's not my fault! Please let me explain, Matriarch Babel...
Please... Please! Give me one more chance, Matriarch... My Lady! I will prove my loyalty to the Tanit... Please believe me... I would gladly offer my life...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: She who knocked your teeth out can also remove your tongue.
...! No, please don't...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I don't understand... If you're willing to give your life for the Tanit, why are you still standing before me, alive?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And another thing... Why did you address me as "My Lady"?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I don't speak the language of the snowlands, and I do not care for the sophistry of the so-called "civilized world"... There is no such thing as "My Lady" here.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And do enlighten me. What makes you think I'm not your family anymore... but some "Lady"?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Your tongue is tainted with outsider poison, your mind stained by their gold. You cannot remain here.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I shall speak no further. Lead him away... He was once one of us, so you know what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The weeping man is taken away, leaving an uneasy silence...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a while, the crowd begins to disperse, making room for you to see the Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh, what just happened...? Whatever it was, it sounded scary!)

choices.text: (I'd hate to get on her bad side...)

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yes...?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ah... My apologies, children. I was a little distracted. I forgot you were there.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I'm terribly sorry that you had to see... that. I'm at fault. As the Matriarch of the Tanit, I'd like to make amends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, n—no need! Y'know, what with that "teeth and tongue" stuff and all...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Heh... We were simply meting out punishment against a traitor. All the same, I am sorry for having given you such a terrible first impression as Matriarch.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: The city has its laws, and the tribe has its rules — please, do not pay it too much mind.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: #So you two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yes? Jeht talks about you two a lot.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We came to look for Jeht.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This doesn't seem like a good time, though.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ah, no need to be so polite! Indeed, I should say that you have impeccable timing.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: It was I who approved her invitation in the first place. That is how you got safely past the Tanit's hunting grounds.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Hehe. While I do feel bad saying this... I invited you here to help Jeht with some unfinished business.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Hunting Grounds"?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Don't worry. We weren't trying to hunt you. You are an honored guest here. For so long as we remember our guests' faces, we shall never do them harm on our land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That still isn't very reassuring...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Haha. Now then, don't let me spoil the fun for you young folks... Look, Jeht is here.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Matriarch Babel, I have returned.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: How did it go with that fellow?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I made sure that he was given sufficient dignity.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: ...That's good. But do not be proud of this deed, child. This was a tragic affair. He was my tribesman, and yours also.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Yeah.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Haha, alright. This is not a good day to preach. The friends you have been waiting for have finally arrived, so set your tears aside and greet them with joy.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Matriarch Babel? What do you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Long time no see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Jeht! We're here to see you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! And Paimon, too! You really did come!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thank you, Matriarch Babel! I shouldn't have gotten mad at everyone about it...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Now, now, of course I'm happy to see you all together. Whatever it is that you want to see or do, I've already approved it. You can put your doubts to rest.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: A word of caution, however... The road ahead of you will be fraught with danger and intrigue, so be on your guard. Please stay safe...

response.speaker: Messenger
response.text: Matriarch Babel, Azariq has sent me to deliver a message to you.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Understood...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: If you'll excuse me, I have tribal affairs to attend to. I'll leave you young ones to catch up.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thanks!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Babel hurries away together with the messenger.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht, you've changed a lot since we last saw you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hehe, got a good eye, haven't you, Paimon? So, what's different about me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You look a little more tanned...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hey! Mouthy as always, huh!?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Is that so? Hehe, after all we've been through, one probably should mature, even if just a little.}{F#I—Is that so? Uh, I thought you were gonna make fun of me or something...}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right. You look like you've really come into your own.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Really? I just learned a lot of survival skills here, that's all. Been busy keeping myself alive, you know?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Matriarch Babel has taken good care of me all this time, and I've helped her out with a lot of things... I'm grateful that she's accepted me as a member of the tribe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And have you been doing well since we last met?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Hehe, did you think I was pining after you like some lovesick maiden?}{F#Hardly. Not a moment has passed since then that I haven't thought of you.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Hang on a moment! Where did you learn to say all that?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hahahaha! Aw, and here I thought I'd get you to blush!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I'm kidding, I'm kidding. All the boys in the tribe are like that, talking nonsense like this... It's annoying. They can't beat me anyway.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ahem... To be honest, it's been tough living, but we're all looking out for each other and helping each other out, so we can all survive.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Still, the first days were rough, and I occasionally thought about the days back when my father would teach and protect me... Hehe, and to think that I used to find him annoying when he was around.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But the good old days won't put food on the table today, and Matriarch Babel and the rest of the Tanit have been taking good care of me... so it's better to look ahead.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Since the Tanit have accepted me, I'm learning to make myself more useful to everyone.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Anyway, let's not dally. I've got some errands to run, and since you're here, why not join me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, is that what you do with old friends?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hehe, sorry, sorry. People are just busy sometimes, you know?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hmm... let me think. Yuften needs help feeding the crocodiles, so let's go there first!

talks.objective: Katheryne seems to be looking for you...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hello there. We have a letter for you — it's from Ms. Jeht.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? So you know Jeht, too, Katheryne? How's she doing?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The Adventurers' Guild has an open partnership with the Eremites, so it would be more surprising if I didn't know her. She looked quite happy when she arrived, and said she was looking forward to seeing you again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Interesting. Let's see what Jeht's written, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Looks like she's having a good time. Better than the last time we saw each other!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, what's this? "The Tanit camp"? That name sorta rings a bell. Have we been there before?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The Tanit are the tribe from which Jeht hails. Their campsite is in the depths of Deshret Desert, amidst the ruins of what was once the city of Gurabad. If you don't mind, I'll mark it out on your map.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Katheryne really is a walking, breathing encyclopedia...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: #You flatter me, {NICKNAME}. In order to better serve adventurers, it is the duty of the Adventurers' Guild to provide such basic information whenever it is needed.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: And the Tanit have always had good commercial relations with the Adventurers' Guild. With Ms. Jeht as our point of contact, they have proven themselves reliable across many acts of cooperation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... The letter also says that she'd like to settle some unfinished business and has expressly asked us to come along. How mysterious... did she mention anything specific, Katheryne?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well, I'm not at liberty to infringe upon the sender's privacy. I'm afraid the only way you'll find out is if you pay her a visit in person.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, there's information that even you can't get a hold of, huh?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Sorry. This isn't a matter of ability or lack thereof, but a matter of professionalism. We do not accept any complaints on this front.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The Tanit campsite has been marked on your map for you. They'll be settling there for the next two or three years, as is the custom of tribal migration.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If they happen to not be at this location, please do not hesitate to contact me. I will update you concerning their migratory pattern as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that's real thoughtful of you, but Paimon doesn't think we're gonna wait two to three years to go look for Jeht...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Okay, {NICKNAME}. Now that we know where Jeht is, what are we waiting for? Let's not keep her waiting!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: In that case, do contact her for more specific information... Oh, sorry. I forgot to mention that this is not a guild commission. It should just be a meeting between friends...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Anyway, ad astra abyssosque! May your reunion lead to new happy encounters and adventures!

choices.text: Well, you'd expect this of the well-informed Adventurers' Guild.

talks.objective: Go to the Tanit tribe and find Jeht

dialogues.speaker: Tanit Tribe Scout
dialogues.text: Hey! Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: A letter? Show me.

dialogues.text: You give Jeht's letter to the scout for review...

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Well, if you're Jeht's friends, I won't stop you. You may move on. The tribe's campsite lies ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Jeht isn't back yet, but Aderfi, Masseira, and Yuften are in at the moment. They're pretty friendly to outsiders.

dialogues.speaker: Mendas
dialogues.text: Don't hesitate to seek them out... But if you dare deceive us, you will find us quite unfriendly indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Hello, young ones. What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... We're here to see Jeht. Is she around?

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Jeht? Yes... she's here. Why are you looking for her?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're her friends.

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Friends...? Oh.

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: #She's mentioned you before, I think. Something about a "brave and reliable {M#young man}{F#young woman}." Hmph, she's been hanging around outside for too long, I see, to be making friends with rich people in fancy clothing and such.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's that supposed to mean!?

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Sorry for speaking so rudely, but I care little for receiving outsiders. You should seek out Matriarch Babel instead.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: She's a good kid.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: What do you mean "so"? She's a good kid. I don't want to see her come under the bad influence of outsiders. Like I said before, if you need anything, seek out Matriarch Babel. Don't bother me.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Well, I have nothing much else to say to you... Why don't you go find Masseira? He's a strange old man. Who knows, maybe you'll get a warmer welcome there.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: What do I do? I do business, exchanging our trash for trash from the city.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: #Hello. {NICKNAME}, I presume?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Shh... Let me guess... You're here to find someone. Your friend, yes?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, but...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Jeht is a good girl. I'm glad she has a friend like you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Hehe. Anyway, if you don't mind a little advice... You look like a real killer, that you do. But "companions"? Those will prove to be your undoing... Your fatal weakness.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't understand what you're trying to say...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Then consider my words but a breeze in your ear. Hmm... Matriarch Babel's not back yet, so you can go talk to Yuften. He's right by the creek where we raise crocodiles. You can't miss it.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Hello, stranger. What d—do you need?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Oh, the M—Matriarch told me about you. You're good folk.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: If you're looking for Jeht, sh—she's still out... Please go to meet Matriarch Babel first. She has b—been waiting for you for a long time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About Jeht...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: She's a good kid.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And...?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: She's made friends, is very happy, and talks like a l—l—little antelope... I'm very... very happy for her.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Hmm, it's getting busy up there. Matriarch Babel has returned. O—okay, you should probably meet her. Please don't keep her w—waiting too long.

choices.text: Hello... do you need any help?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Huh? I d—don't need... Why are you asking?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Oh, you mean the way I t—talk, right?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Haha... I'm used t—to it, and I hope you will be, too. Speaking a little slower makes your train of th—thought all the clearer.

dialogues.text: B—But... I don't know what those outsiders wanted... It's not my fault! Please let me explain, Matriarch Babel...
Please... Please! Give me one more chance, Matriarch... My Lady! I will prove my loyalty to the Tanit... Please believe me... I would gladly offer my life...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: She who knocked your teeth out can also remove your tongue.
...! No, please don't...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I don't understand... If you're willing to give your life for the Tanit, why are you still standing before me, alive?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And another thing... Why did you address me as "My Lady"?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I don't speak the language of the snowlands, and I do not care for the sophistry of the so-called "civilized world"... There is no such thing as "My Lady" here.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: And do enlighten me. What makes you think I'm not your family anymore... but some "Lady"?

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Your tongue is tainted with outsider poison, your mind stained by their gold. You cannot remain here.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I shall speak no further. Lead him away... He was once one of us, so you know what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The weeping man is taken away, leaving an uneasy silence...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a while, the crowd begins to disperse, making room for you to see the Matriarch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh, what just happened...? Whatever it was, it sounded scary!)

choices.text: (I'd hate to get on her bad side...)

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Hmm...?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ah... My apologies, children. I was a little distracted. I forgot you were there.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I'm terribly sorry that you had to see... that. I'm at fault. As the Matriarch of the Tanit, I'd like to make amends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, n—no need! Y'know, what with that "teeth and tongue" stuff and all...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Heh... We were simply meting out punishment against a traitor. All the same, I am sorry for having given you such a terrible first impression as Matriarch.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: The city has its laws, and the tribe has its rules — please, do not pay it too much mind.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: #So you two are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yes? Jeht talks about you two a lot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This doesn't seem like a good time, though.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ah, no need to be so polite! Indeed, I should say that you have impeccable timing.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: It was I who approved her invitation in the first place. That is how you got safely past the Tanit's hunting grounds.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Hehe. While I do feel bad saying this... I invited you here to help Jeht with some unfinished business.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Hunting Grounds"?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Don't worry. We weren't trying to hunt you. You are an honored guest here. For so long as we remember our guests' faces, we shall never do them harm on our land.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That still isn't very reassuring...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Haha. Now then, don't let me spoil the fun for you young folks... Look, Jeht is here.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Matriarch Babel, I have returned.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: How did it go with that fellow?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I made sure that he was given sufficient dignity.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: ...That's good. But do not be proud of this deed, child. This was a tragic affair. He was my tribesman, and yours also.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Haha, alright. This is not a good day to preach. The friends you have been waiting for have finally arrived, so set your tears aside and greet them with joy.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Matriarch Babel? What do you...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Long time no see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Jeht! We're here to see you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! And Paimon, too! You really did come!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thank you, Matriarch Babel! I shouldn't have gotten mad at everyone about it...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Now, now, of course I'm happy to see you all together. Whatever it is that you want to see or do, I've already approved it. You can put your doubts to rest.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: A word of caution, however... The road ahead of you will be fraught with danger and intrigue, so be on your guard. Please stay safe...

response.speaker: Messenger
response.text: Matriarch Babel, Azariq has sent me to deliver a message to you.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Understood...

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: If you'll excuse me, I have tribal affairs to attend to. I'll leave you young ones to catch up.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thanks!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Babel hurries away together with the messenger.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht, you've changed a lot since we last saw you!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hehe, got a good eye, haven't you, Paimon? So, what's different about me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You look a little more tanned...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hey! Mouthy as always, huh!?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Is that so? Hehe, after all we've been through, one probably should mature, even if just a little.}{F#I—Is that so? Uh, I thought you were gonna make fun of me or something...}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s right. You look like you've really come into your own.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Really? I just learned a lot of survival skills here, that's all. Been busy keeping myself alive, you know?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Matriarch Babel has taken good care of me all this time, and I've helped her out with a lot of things... I'm grateful that she's accepted me as a member of the tribe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And have you been doing well since we last met?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Hehe, did you think I was pining after you like some lovesick maiden?}{F#Hardly. Not a moment has passed since then that I haven't thought of you.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Hang on a moment! Where did you learn to say all that?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hahahaha! Aw, and here I thought I'd get you to blush!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I'm kidding, I'm kidding. All the boys in the tribe are like that, talking nonsense like this... It's annoying. They can't beat me anyway.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ahem... To be honest, it's been tough living, but we're all looking out for each other and helping each other out, so we can all survive.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Still, the first days were rough, and I occasionally thought about the days back when my father would teach and protect me... Hehe, and to think that I used to find him annoying when he was around.

response.speaker: Jeht

response.speaker: Jeht

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Anyway, let's not dally. I've got some errands to run, and since you're here, why not join me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, is that what you do with old friends?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hehe, sorry, sorry. People are just busy sometimes, you know?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hmm... let me think. Yuften needs help feeding the crocodiles, so let's go there first!

choices.text: We came to look for her.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #I'm here, Yuften! And I've brought my friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: H—Hello, Jeht. Have you finished your b—b—business?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yep, and that's why I thought I should come here to help you out, and brought my friends along to boot!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Oh? Thank you, Jeht. You r—r—remembered that I had something I needed your help with!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Haha. Back when Elder Bleda was around, you used to pester him to f—f—feed the crocodiles together with you...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ahem...! Loose lips sink ships!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Um, alright... Here's the f—f—food. The meat's fresh. Take it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Okay! Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Feed the crocodiles together with Jeht

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Feeding crocodiles is pretty easy... You drop the meat, they follow the scent, and they eat it themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, your Matriarch seems pretty fearsome...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean what happened just now? Well, it's nothing. We were just dealing with a traitor.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I tracked him through the desert for half a month before bringing him back alive. He was crafty, and plenty fierce to boot. I had to knock some of his teeth out to subdue him... Argh, my hand still hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... that sounds scary...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So be careful what you say around me in the future, eh, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Watch your teeth, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't be so serious! We're all friends here. I'm just kidding!

talks.objective: Feed the crocodiles together with Jeht

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It does look like you're taken seriously around here... Everyone seems to respect you!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, here's the thing... Because of my previous experience with adventurers, I'm more perceptive about things that happen outside the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So the Matriarch decided that it would be my job to track down outsiders and punish traitors to the tribe.

choices.text: She's taking good care of you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Since I wasn't born amongst the Tanit, it's okay for me to deal with criminals in a more aggressive way... That's what Matriarch Babel told me.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Although I don't really care... I'm not sure if this is a special privilege or proof of our estrangement.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, I wasn't born here, after all, and the Tanit tribe isn't a home I'm innately familiar with. I can only try my best to do everything well. As long as I can put some roots down, I think I'll be fine.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It's okay... I'm just trying to survive around here, and I've learned a lot, too.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright, I think they've eaten their fill. Let's go!

choices.text: It's good to see that you've finally found a home.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, don't laugh, now, but I'm glad to see you here.

choices.text: Why has she entrusted this work to you?

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: H—Have you finished, Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah. I'm going to wash now! Your crocodile food stinks — smells of raw meat!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Haha... And d—does that or traitor-blood smell worse?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hey! Not funny!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Thank you. By the way... th—there's one more thing that I want to a—ask of you...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: This is the cured c—c—crocodile meat that I promised to give Aderfi previously. Pass it on to him for me, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sure, sure, I'll give your c—c—crocodile meat to Aderfi, no problem!

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: H—Hey! Th—that was uncalled for!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hahaha, smell ya later!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I'm here, Aderfi!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Oh? Here to show off your new outsider friends?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sort of! By the way, here's the crocodile jerky from Yuften!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Ah, thanks. You're so considerate...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hehe, no worries! By the way, about Benben... can you still fix it?

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Don't worry, it's nothing serious. I'll be able to get it back to you in a couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh... okay! Then I'll get going!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Heh... running here and there really works up a sweat...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, it's fine. I don't like being idle, actually.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ah, but look at me. I didn't invite you guys here so you could come run errands with me!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, so here's the story: Matriarch Babel recently agreed to let me bring Dad's... my father's remains, and those of my mother, to be buried in the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? So that's a real place? Paimon thought that it was just a myth.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, the last time we parted, I was so lost... I honestly didn't know where to start looking for it. Matriarch Babel, however, seems very sure that the Eternal Oasis lies in the middle of this desert...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The Tanit tribe holds that the never-ending sandstorm at the heart of the desert conceals the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Unfortunately, that area has been sealed off by the tribe as a taboo place. No one can approach except scouts on patrol.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Taboo...? Is it dangerous or something?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yes. Some older folks believe that ancient spirits roam there, hungering for souls and flesh... But that's probably just a myth. I don't believe it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah, but I'm not afraid. I've seen lots of spooky stuff in my time. As long as my blade can strike it, I'm not afraid of it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: As for things my blade can't strike, we'll just have to outrun it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Basically, I can bypass the taboos of the elders and explore the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That'll let me fulfill a long-cherished wish of mine, and secure the future of the tribe too. They believe that this is where the secrets of the mistress of flowers lie.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If these secrets can be discovered... They'll give the tribe a new lease on life!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I know that this is my duty and honor. But I've been thinking, and I've been getting this feeling that I should invite you to witness it with me.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: After all... since my father passed, that leaves you as my most trusted friends... the closest thing I have to family right now. That's why I wanted to ask you to join me on this wayward little trip of mine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht... You can rest easy. Of course we'll help!

choices.text: We won't let a friend down.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thanks so much, you guys!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ahem... First, we need to go to the ruins of Gurabad to look for this "Jinni Fragment" thing...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I don't quite understand it, but the tribe's stories say that she's the only one who knows how to open the way to the Oasis, so we'll have to find her...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Umm... And that's all I can tell you, really. I think Azariq can tell you more. So... Shall we go?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Okay, then we're off! I have so many other things I wanna say!

choices.text: I don't feel like leaving just yet...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, if you want to hang around a little more, that's fine. I'm here. Whenever you want to go, I'll be right behind you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Heh... Having you around really puts me at ease. Azariq's supposed to be waiting for us at the Gurabad ruins, so let's take a break first before heading out, shall we?

choices.text: We didn't come all this way just to leave, you know.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hahaha, I knew you'd say that! You won't go unrewarded, rest assured!

choices.text: Why has Babel given you special permission, if I might ask?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It's probably on account of that "afraid-of-nothing" attitude of mine that Matriarch Babel has taken special care of me...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: And it might also be because... I'm a "half-outsider," so I'm able to forego some of the taboos that the elders valued... That's what I think, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well? Are you ready to go?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Okay, let's move out!

choices.text: Not yet. I still want to rest a bit.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Be my guest. If you need anything, come to me anytime!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: My father always dreamed of that place. I didn't know my mother very well... But she also kept records of it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: They said they wanted to live in this place for the rest of their lives... So it must be an oasis of dreamlike beauty, I think.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hey, don't laugh at me for my rudimentary knowledge. I followed my dad on adventures and saw some impressive sights, but this was the only one that stuck with him...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I wonder what kind of place it is...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alas... Haha, it's no use getting upset now. We'll find out when we step outside together!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well, come back to me when you're ready to go!

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. I've got my work to do, and you've got yours. There's no need to look around here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: If you need to see Jeht, you'll have to wait for Matriarch Babel... Why, you ask? Well, you'll see...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: G—Go see the Matriarch. I'm sure she and Jeht will be very h—happy to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you...

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: You've already met the Matriarch? If you haven't gotten kicked out, that means you're our honored guest... Well, feel free to wander as you like, then.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Hmm? You've got a good eye, I must say. Yes, I am indeed a merchant. I sell the various things that the tribe lacks. Cosmetics, luxury items, costumes, toys, agricultural products, intricate tools...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: What would you like? If you should need something, I'll have it. And if I don't, just tell me what you need, and I'll get it for you, whether it's from the city, or even from Fontaine!

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Ah... Right, you're an outsider. Well, in that case, you have my apologies, but my shop is not open to you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've got lots of books here. May I read them?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: The books? Oh! Right, those are here at the request of Matriarch Babel. I'm sure you've heard, and seen, that the city people have taken to using this thing called the Akasha, which they mount on their ears.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Their libraries have been emptied of a great number of obsolete books, and the Matriarch had me purchase and safe-keep them for everyone to read free of charge. Hmph... I operated at a loss there.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: As for the Akasha, we did ship a set in from another tribe, but it was... very inconvenient to use, not to mention quite arcane indeed. We could not disassemble or repair it, for the wiring was too centralized...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Whatever the case, I'd say that reading books on your own is far better than relying on some strange machine to stuff information into your brain.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: After all, who knows what back doors you might open if you just let people into the door of your mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Don't let me get in your way.

choices.text: What are you selling here, anyway?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Straight to the point, hmm? I like buyers like you. Unfortunately, I don't sell to outsiders.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Um, this is not due to xenophobia or some kind of base prejudice. It's more that... Our tribe and the merchants in the cities don't share economic spheres, if you can glean my meaning?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I only serve the Tanit tribe, you know, as our exclusive distributer of goods. All trade and other transactions have to go through Matriarch Babel, and I take a small cut of that.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Spoken to Babel, have you? Ah, she's probably busying herself somewhere else again... You would sooner stop the wind than stop her.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Haha... You know, youngster, speaking of the wind... I'd like to remind you of a kind of desert wind that we call "Zibri."

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: At first, you won't sense anything, until the sandstorm rises over the horizon, and the air itself begins to ascend and burn. Only then will you realize...

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: ...That you can no longer smell anything, for the heated air has smothered your sense of smell, seared your nostrils...

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: By then... Heh. By then, it will be too late.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I didn't catch your drift...

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: It's nothing... I just mean to say that you should be careful of the sandstorms.

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Those crocodiles are a v—very gentle... Still, be careful when you feed them...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Watch your fingers...

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you.

dialogues.speaker: Aderfi
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel mentioned you previously, honored guest. Please, have a look around.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Hmm...? I thought I had already introduced myself... I sell the various things that the tribe lacks. Cosmetics, luxury items, costumes, toys, agricultural products, intricate tools...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: What would you like? If you should need something, I'll have it. And if I don't, just tell me what you need, and I'll get it for you, whether it's from the city, or even from Fontaine!

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Ah... Right, you're an outsider. Well, in that case, you have my apologies, but my shop is not open to you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've got lots of books here. May I read them?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Books? ...Oh, right, you mean the ones Matriarch Babel requested... See, it's been fashionable for city people to wear Akasha on their ears for some time. You must have seen them.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Their libraries have been emptied of a great number of obsolete books, and the Matriarch had me purchase and safe-keep them for everyone to read free of charge. Hmph... I operated at a loss there.

response.speaker: Aderfi

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Whatever the case, I'd say that reading books on your own is far better than relying on some strange machine to stuff information into your brain.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: After all, who knows what back doors you might open if you just let people into the door of your mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Don't let me get in your way.

choices.text: What are you selling here, anyway?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Straight to the point, hmm? I like buyers like you. Unfortunately, I don't sell to outsiders.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Um, this is not due to xenophobia or some kind of base prejudice. It's more that... Our tribe and the merchants in the cities don't share economic spheres, if you can glean my meaning?

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I only serve the Tanit tribe, you know, as our exclusive distributer of goods. All trade and other transactions have to go through Matriarch Babel, and I take a small cut of that.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Of course, you are our guest, so you can feel free to take whatever catches your eye here in my tent... Uh, as long as you don't take it all, anyway.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Benben... Ah, you mean the little machine that follows Jeht around.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I've examined it before. There's nothing particularly wrong with it, but as for how it can be restored to its former, energetic state...

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: I have my ways... but I don't think I could tell you.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Whatever the case, I think it's best that it stays with me till the repairs are done.

response.speaker: Aderfi
response.text: Anything else you'd like to ask me?

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: Hello... Guest of Tanit...

dialogues.speaker: Yuften
dialogues.text: J—J—Jeht mentions you often. She's a good kid.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Planting crops and f—feeding the fish. Sometimes, I also do some b—b—butchery. Crocodile skin and meat is v—very useful.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: We get clean spring water all year around h—here, so it's just right for raising crocodiles. Th—that's why we fenced this place up.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Crocodiles are easy to care for, and they can be harvested for lots of skins and meat. Unfortunately, f—fields are a d—different story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You have fields around here?

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: We do... but only for testing. Matriarch Babel invited some outsiders to c—c—come and provide us with Anahitian Blessing, and she got all these old books from the city...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: S—s—so we've tried our hand at farming according to the contents of these books.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: But the oases in the canyon are too narrow and lack nutrients. We need to find a way to f—fertilize the soil.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tell me about the Anahitian Blessing...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: The outsiders didn't want to reveal the fertilizer's composition. As such, we've had to rely on the people who provide it to f—fertilize the soil... which isn't good.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Th—that's why the Matriarch wants me to d—do some research here to r—reverse engineer our own Anahitian Blessing.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I shan't disturb you any longer.

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Th—that's alright. Please take some crocodile jerky, dear guest. It's just over there...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: Hehe, yes. I—I take care of them. These are quite large and obedient...

response.speaker: Yuften
response.text: This one's c—c—called Sedim. Very fierce and strong, and skin's very vibrant. It'll make for a good satchel. And there's that one, Karam. It's small but plump. Rather gentle, too.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}! If it's convenient, there's a message for you here!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Come with me. Don't let the crocodiles bite your foot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Unlike in the rainforest, the crocodiles here are docile and much smaller.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: They've sacrificed a lot to adapt to living in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Aderfi has a lot of nice stuff that you can't find or trade, and people like to go there to do business.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Y'know, to get things like... gadgets, toys, new clothes... and cosmetics...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Do you wear makeup?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What do you even mean by that? Lapis lazuli eye shadow is an essential sunscreen for us desert folk, and we can use concealer to hide scars. Makeup's super useful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so that's it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You arrive at a canyon, but your path has been barred...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hehe... It's good that you were able to come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're glad to see you too, Jeht! There's so much we'd like to tell you, but... Hmm, where should we even begin?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I know, right? There's so much we all want to say, but now that we've met... Hehe, "where should we start," huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I've learned a phrase here in the tribe, and it goes something like "the closer your home, the more reticent your heart." And, y'know, it describes our situation perfectly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, is this tribe always so... er, eloquent?
